messages.subject: Important ISEC dates and information
messages.body_plain:
Hello friends and colleagues (and apologies for cross posting!),

Here is some information and important dates as we creep closer to ISEC24. The links and information for the items below will start appearing on the new ISEC website over the next two weeks (https://statisticalecology.org/, the dedicated website for ISEC conferences from now on).

Please share this information with your friends, colleagues, and students.

Looking forward to seeing you all in Swansea in the summer

Luca and the ISEC organising committee.

ISEC2024: The International Statistical Ecology Conference

15th – 19th July 2024

Swansea, UK

Keynote Speaker

We are excited to announce that we have confirmed a fantastic collection of keynote speakers for the conference this year (details on the website):

Dr. Marie Auger-Méthé (University of British Columbia, Canada)
Prof. John Fieberg (University of Minnesota, USA)
Prof. Rachel McCrea (Lancaster University, UK)
Dr. Matthew Schofield (University of Otago, NZ)
Dr. Elise Zipkin (Michigan State University, USA)

Registration and accommodation

Registration will open in the next 2 weeks with a registration deadline of 15th June. There will be a ‘standard delegate rate’ and a (reduced) ‘student delegate rate’ and the costs will be in line with previous rates. There will be no ‘early bird’ rate.  We have arranged a block booking for on-site university accommodation. These rooms will be held until the end of April, which is after decisions will be announced about abstracts (see below). This accommodation is, of course, optional.

Abstract submission

Abstract submission will open in the next 2 weeks and will close on Friday 22nd of March. Abstract will be submitted vias the website (link to appear soon). Decisions about abstracts will be communicated by early April. There will be standard talks and posters.

Workshops

We are now welcoming proposals for workshops! If you are interested in proposing a workshop, please send the following information to Luca Borger (l.borger [at] swansea.ac.uk <http://swansea.ac.uk>) and Chris Sutherland (css6 [at] st-andrews.ac.uk <http://st-andrews.ac.uk>):
Title
Short workshop description (<300 word)
Intended audience
Whether you are proposing a ½ day or a full day workshop
We will charge a small fee for workshops which will be used to cover the registration of workshop instructors and refreshments.

Chris

While I may be sending this email outside of my normal office hours, I have no expectation to receive a reply outside of yours.

Chris Sutherland (he/him/his)

Reader

Centre for Research into Ecological & Environmental Modelling

School of Mathematics and Statistics
University of St Andrews

W: website <https://www.sutherlandecology.com/>

E: cs...@st-andrews.ac.uk

messages.subject: oSCR Challenges with single-sex data
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am using oSCR for the first time and have been getting the hang of it, but have been struggling to get more solid estimates when some of my datasets only have one sex present (most often males, the animal I am studying has very low populations).

In this scenario, I often get results like this:

# Model:  D ~ 1 p0 ~ 1 sig ~ 1
# Run time:  0.01688333  minutes
# AIC:  151.8773
#
# Summary table:
#                   Estimate      SE       z P(>|z|)
# p0.(Intercept)    -3.603   0.264 -13.662   0.000
# sig.(Intercept)   21.098     NaN     NaN     NaN
# d0.(Intercept)    -2.738   0.500  -5.472   0.000
# psi.constant     -20.066 838.861  -0.024   0.981
# *Density intercept is log(individuals per pixel)
# Nhat(state-space) = exp(d0.)*nrow(ssDF)
# (caution is warranted when model contains density covariates)

#make predictions on the real scale
(DA2015_pred.dens2 <- get.real(DA20151.scr0, type = "dens", newdata = DA2015_pred.df.dens))
#         estimate           se        lwr       upr Session sex
# 1  6.470319e-02 3.237524e-02 0.02426644 0.1725223       1   f
# 11 1.248165e-10 1.047037e-07 0.00000000       Inf       1   m

Is this to be expected and is there anything that can be done to get more realistic estimates for the population of either sex?

If not, are there any other packages that may be more suited to these camera trap analyses for population density and size estimates, etc?

These are all with single-session analyses, I am just about to start using multi-session analyses.

Many thanks,
Jamie

messages.subject: Error in ms$coef.tab
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have been running multi-session models on my data, following along with the workflow on the multi-session model PDF on the oSCR website - "getting started with oSCR" page (https://sites.google.com/site/spatialcapturerecapture/oscr-package/2-getting-started-with-oscr?authuser=0)

ModSel works totally fine as shown below as does ms$aic.tab, but when I look at the ms$coef.tab, none of the coefficients are labelled as such, instead being "NA.1", etc, but there are still values in the rows of these NA columns. Does anyone know if I have miscoded something or if this is a bug, and how I can distinguish which NA column might be which coefficient?

Cheers!
Jamie
